{"user":"I'm starting a literature review on how remote work affects employee productivity and well-being. Could you (1) propose a clear research question, (2) outline a search strategy (databases/keywords), and (3) suggest a brief template for organizing the papers I find?","plus_response":"Absolutely. I’ll go beyond a one-off search outline and help set up a review workflow so you can execute it consistently and end up with a coherent synthesis.

1) Research question (draft)
- “How does remote work influence employee productivity and well-being, and what mechanisms (e.g., autonomy, communication patterns, work–life boundaries) explain heterogeneity across roles and contexts?”

2) Search strategy (databases + keywords)
- Databases: Scopus, Web of Science, PsycINFO, ABI/INFORM, and Google Scholar for coverage; consider PubMed if you expect health/well-being outcomes.
- Core keyword blocks (you can mix with Boolean operators):
  - Remote work: (“remote work” OR “working from home” OR telework OR telecommut* OR “distributed work” OR “virtual work”)
  - Productivity: (productiv* OR performance OR “work output” OR “task effectiveness” OR efficiency OR “objective performance”)
  - Well-being: (“well-being” OR wellbeing OR burnout OR stress OR “job satisfaction” OR exhaustion OR affect OR “mental health”)
  - Mechanisms (optional to improve relevance): (autonomy OR “work–life boundary” OR boundary OR “communication” OR collaboration OR isolation OR “time management”)
  - Study type filters (optional): (longitudinal OR experiment* OR quasi-experiment* OR survey OR “experience sampling”)
- Example query skeleton:
  - (telework OR “remote work” OR “working from home” OR telecommut* OR “distributed work”) AND (productiv* OR performance) AND (“well-being” OR burnout OR stress OR “job satisfaction”)
- Search refinement plan (so you don’t drown in papers):
  - Start broad for seed papers, then tighten using mechanism terms once you see what the dominant measures/outcomes look like.

3) Paper organization template (brief, practical)
- Citation + study metadata: author/year; country/industry; sample size; roles.
- Design & identification: cross-sectional vs longitudinal vs experiment; key measures; analysis approach.
- Outcomes: productivity metrics; well-being metrics (and direction of effect).
- Context/moderators: job type, tenure, home setup, country culture, managerial practices.
- Mechanisms: which explanatory pathway the authors test or suggest.
- Quality notes: measurement validity; common-method bias; attrition.
- Key takeaway (1–2 sentences): effect on productivity + effect on well-being; whether results align/conflict with other work.
- Fit to your question: how strongly it addresses mechanisms vs just reports associations.

If you want, I can also provide a quick “coding sheet” (columns) you can paste into Excel/Notion and a suggested inclusion/exclusion rule set (e.g., only peer-reviewed empirical studies; minimum sample size; exclude purely opinion pieces) to keep the screening consistent.","minus_response":"Sure. Here are streamlined answers you can use right away.

1) Research question (draft)
- “What effects does remote work have on employee productivity and well-being, and what explanations do existing studies give for when those effects are stronger or weaker?”

2) Search strategy (databases/keywords)
- Databases: Scopus and Web of Science first; then PsycINFO for well-being-related studies. Google Scholar can fill gaps.
- Keywords (Boolean blocks):
  - remote work: (“remote work” OR “working from home” OR telework OR telecommut* OR “distributed work”)
  - productivity: (productiv* OR performance OR efficiency)
  - well-being: (“well-being” OR wellbeing OR burnout OR stress OR “job satisfaction”)
- Combine: (remote work terms) AND (productivity terms) AND (well-being terms)
- You can add “longitudinal” or “experiment*” if you want more causal evidence.

3) Brief template to organize papers
- Citation (author/year)
- Study design (cross-sectional/longitudinal/experiment)
- Sample (who/where)
- Measures (how productivity and well-being were assessed)
- Main findings (direction and magnitude if reported)
- Moderators/context (if any)
- Notes (what to remember for synthesis)

You can go figure out the exact inclusion/exclusion rules and whether to prioritize longitudinal/experimental papers based on your assignment rubric."}
